question: What is the landing distance requirement for a Class B aeroplane at the destination and any alternate?

options.text: A full stop from 35 ft within 70% of the LDA
A full stop within the LDA plus any stopway
A full stop from 50 ft within 60% of the LDA
A full stop from 50 ft within 70% of the LDA

explanation: The landing mass must allow a full-stop landing from 50 ft above the threshold within 70% of the landing distance available.

question: Which factor converts a Class B landing distance into the required LDA?
explanation: 1 ÷ 0.7 ≈ 1.43. 1.67 (1 ÷ 0.6) is the factor for jets.

question: The LDA is 2 400 ft. What is the greatest gross landing distance allowed for a Class B aeroplane?
A Class B aeroplane has a gross landing distance of 1 300 ft. What is the shortest LDA that meets the requirement?
If a Class B aeroplane cannot stop within 70% of the LDA, which action would help?
explanation: The landing distance can be reduced by a higher flap setting or a lower landing mass.

question: What does the 70% landing rule illustrate about gross and net performance?

options.text: They are the same for Class B
The net (worst-case) distance is the gross distance × 1.43
The net distance is 70% of the gross distance
The gross distance includes the factor

explanation: The gross distance is the average expected; multiplied by 1.43 it gives the net distance, the "one in a million" worst case that must fit in the LDA.

question: Which temperature is assumed in the Class B gross landing distance calculation?
explanation: The gross landing distance takes account of pressure altitude and standard temperature, as well as surface, slope, factored wind and the despatch rules.

question: What factor is applied to the landing distance for grass up to 20 cm long on firm soil?
explanation: Grass increases the landing distance by 15% (factor 1.15). The take-off grass factors are 1.2 dry and 1.3 wet.

question: What factor is applied to the landing distance if the runway may be wet at the estimated time of arrival?
explanation: A wet runway factor of 1.15 applies; if the flight manual gives specific wet runway data, that may be used even if it gives a shorter distance.

question: What correction is applied for slope in the Class B landing calculation?
explanation: A downslope lengthens the landing, so 5% is added per 1%. No reduction is allowed for an upslope.

question: What landing slope factor applies to a 2% downslope?
explanation: 5% per 1% downslope: 2% gives 1.10.

question: A gross landing distance of 1 200 ft on a dry paved level runway must be corrected for dry grass and a 1% downslope. What is the corrected distance?
explanation: 1 200 × 1.15 × 1.05 ≈ 1 449 ft. Leaving out the slope gives 1 380 ft.

question: Using the corrected landing distance of about 1 450 ft, what is the shortest LDA that meets the Class B requirement?
explanation: 1 449 × 1.43 ≈ 2 070 ft. 1 740 ft would only satisfy a 1.2 factor.

question: What wind components are used in the Class B landing distance calculation?

options.text: Twice the reported headwind and the full tailwind

explanation: As for take-off, headwinds are factored to 50% and tailwinds to 150%. Most landing graphs include this.

question: Which two assumptions must be met for despatch to a destination?

options.text: Landing on the longest runway, and with a 10 kt headwind on that runway
Landing on the runway nearest the terminal
Best runway in still air; likely runway in forecast wind
Landing on any runway in still air only

explanation: It must be assumed the aeroplane lands on the most favourable runway in still air, and on the runway most likely to be assigned given the forecast wind.

question: If the forecast-wind assumption cannot be met at the destination, when may the aeroplane still be despatched?

options.text: If the commander accepts a tailwind landing in writing before departure
If the landing mass is reduced by 5%
If a compliant alternate is designated

explanation: The aeroplane may be despatched only if an alternate aerodrome is designated at which full compliance with the despatch requirements is possible.

question: Still air allows 1 500 kg on the best runway; the forecast wind allows 1 750 kg on the runway likely to be used. What despatch mass may be planned for landing?
explanation: The lower of the two masses must be used, so that landing is possible whatever wind occurs on arrival.

question: When is the forecast-wind landing mass usually lower than the still-air mass?

options.text: On a one-way runway with a tailwind
On any runway with a crosswind
On a long runway with a strong headwind component

explanation: Normally the still-air mass is the lower. The exception is a runway usable in one direction only, where a forecast tailwind reduces the allowed mass below the still-air value.

question: A runway has a 90° crosswind forecast. How does its forecast-wind landing mass compare with its still-air mass?
explanation: A pure crosswind gives no headwind or tailwind component, so the mass is the same as in still air.

question: What is the minimum VREF for a single-engine Class B aeroplane?
explanation: VREF must be no less than 1.3 times the stall speed in the landing configuration. The landing graphs are built on this speed.

question: On a Class B landing graph, what does the left-hand carpet account for?
explanation: The left carpet combines temperature and pressure altitude to account for density; then come mass, wind and the 50 ft "obstacle" carpet.

question: On a landing graph, what does the last carpet, marked "obstacle height", represent?

options.text: The extra stopping distance on a wet runway
A real obstacle on the approach

explanation: The landing starts at 50 ft above the threshold; the last carpet adds the airborne distance from 50 ft to touchdown.

question: On a light twin landing graph, how can the ground roll alone be found?

options.text: By going straight through the last (50 ft) carpet
By reading the left-hand carpet only
By doubling the total landing distance

explanation: Passing straight across the final carpet, instead of following its guidelines up to 50 ft, gives only the ground roll.
